newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ascom boosted 1996 oper profit - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Ascom boosted 1996 oper profit - chairman.

text.p: Swiss telecommunications group Ascom Holding AG boosted 1996 operating profit and could do so again in 1997, company officials said.

"The (1996) operating profit numbers will be good, better than than a year ago and in line with what we said in September," chairman Felix Wittlin told Reuters in an interview at the World Economic Forum in Davos. He gave no details.
Finance chief Jakob Schlapbach also said there was a "slight" decline in order inflow and sales in 1996, but Wittlin said this reflected the company's streamlining efforts.
Schlapbach also forecast operating results would improve in 1997, assuming Ascom can get its enterprise networks division in order.

"I would say we should boost operating results, assuming we can find a good solution for our enterprise networks (division)," he said, referring to the company's efforts to sell or find an investor for its Timeplex division in the U.S.
"We are holding concrete talks. We are talking to partners, we are talking to investors about a positive approach, not just window dressing," Wittlin said.
Ascom said in September that group operating profit for the first half of 1996 was 39 million Swiss francs ($27.4 million), up from 28 million a year earlier.
In 1995 Ascom reported a net profit of 25 million francs compared with 21 million.
Schlapbach said the company would use proceeds of any Timeplex sale to reduce debt, which Wittlin said had been halved to around 500 million Swiss francs by the end of 1996.
"Timeplex does not now look like it looked a year ago," Schlapbach said, having cut around 300 jobs and introduced important products that are gaining a toehold in markets.
"We have a different package to offer a partner," he said.
Wittlin said Timeplex had reached the break-even point in the last financial quarter.
